title: SPA/7/2015 of Hukum Singh Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 07 of 2015
With
Review Application No.1610 of 2018
Delay Condonation Application in Review Application No.19256 of 2018
Hukum Singh .......Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others .......Respondents
Mr. P.S. Bohra, Advocate for the review applicant-petitioner.
Mr. B.P.S. Mer, Brief Holder for the State.
Coram: Hon'ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
 Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.

The application, seeking condonation of the delay in preferring the
review application, is not opposed; and the delay is, therefore, condoned. Delay
condonation application stands disposed of.
Review Application No.1610 of 2018
2. This application is filed seeking review of the order passed by a
Division Bench of this Court in Special Appeal No.07 of 2015 dated 26.09.2018.
3. The review applicant herein filed Writ Petition (S/S) No.45 of 2007
seeking payment of salary for the period he worked as officiating Principal in the
B.D. Inter College, Bhagwanpur, Haridwar district. In his order in Writ Petition
(S/S) No.45 of 2007 dated 01.12.2014, the learned Single Judge observed that the
review applicant herein was given salary for the post of Lecturer; the said amount
was given to him from the funds of the Management Committee; the said institute,
admittedly, was under grant-in-aid only upto Class 10; Classes 11 and 12 were not
under grant-in-aid; any teacher or lecturer ,appointed to teach Classes 11 and 12,
was to be paid from the private funds of the institute; the review applicant was,
admittedly, paid salary by the Managing Committee of the institute since he was
engaged as a lecturer to teach Classes 11 and 12, which post was not admitted to
grant-in-aid; the review applicant's claim that he was the Principal of the entire
institute which was partly under grant-in-aid, and he was therefore entitled to be
paid the salary applicable to the post of Principal, was without any basis; as the
institute was, admittedly, under grant-in-aid only upto Class 10, and not for Classes
11 and 12, and as the review applicant was a teacher of Classes 11 and 12 alone, he
was not entitled to be paid the salary being paid to a Principal; whatever he was

2
entitled, as a Lecturer, was being paid to him; salary of the teachers, who teach in
Classes 11 and 12, were generated from the private funds of the institute; the
review applicant herein was admittedly a teacher of Classes 11 and 12, and was
called upon to discharge the duties of an officiating principal; and, as the lien of
the review applicant herein remained as a teacher of Classes 11 and 12, the State
Exchequer was not liable to make payment.
4. In the appeal preferred there-against i.e. Special Appeal No.07 of
2015, a Division Bench of this Court, in its order dated 26.09.2018, observed that
the review applicant herein was appointed as Lecturer to teach only Classes 11 and
12; the private institute was receiving grant-in-aid only upto matriculation; the
salary of the review applicant came from private funds; and there was no merit in
the Special Appeal.
5. While Mr. P.S. Bohra, learned counsel for the review applicant, would
rely on the definition of an 'institution' under Section 2(b) of the Intermediate
Education Act, 1921, to contend that, even if the review applicant is held to have
been appointed as a lecturer only for a part of the institute, he must be held to be
the Principal of the institute in its entirety; Section 18(2) of the Uttar Pradesh
Secondary Education Services Selection Board Act, 1982 stipulates that where the
management fails to promote the senior most teacher under sub-section (1), the
Inspector shall himself issue an order of promotion of such teacher; and the teacher
concerned shall be entitled to get his salary as the Principal or the Headmaster, as
the case may be, from the date he joins such post pursuant to such an order of
promotion.
6. On the other hand Mr. B.P.S. Mer, learned Brief Holder appearing for
the State Government, would rely on Section 7-AA (5) of the 1921 Act, to contend
that the review applicant can, at best, claim honorarium for the part-time duties
discharged by him; and this amount, representing the honorarium, can only be
claimed from the Managing Committee, and not from the Government.
7. Section 18(1) of the 1982 Act stipulates that, where the Management
has notified a vacancy to the Board in accordance with sub-section (1) of Section
10 and the post of the Principal or the Headmaster actually remained vacant for
more than two months, the Management shall fill such vacancy, on a purely ad hoc

3
basis, by promoting the senior most teacher in the lecturer's grade in respect of a
vacancy in the post of the Principal; and under the trained graduate's grade in
respect of a vacancy in the post of the Headmaster. In terms of Section 18(2) of the
1982 Act, where the Management fails to promote the senior most teacher under
sub-section (1), the Inspector shall himself issue the order of promotion of such
teacher and the teacher concerned shall be entitled to get his salary as the Principal
or the Headmaster, as the case may be, from the date he joins such post pursuant
thereto.
8. The review applicant was, admittedly, appointed as a Lecturer only to
teach Classes 11 and 12. The said Classes 11 and 12 were not admitted to grant-in-aid, and the subject institute was receiving grant-in-aid only upto Class 10. The
review applicant's salary as a Lecturer for Classes 11 and 12 were, admittedly,
being paid by the Managing Committee from its private funds, and not from the
funds received by the Government as grant-in-aid. Section 18(1) of the 1982 Act,
which requires the senior most lecturer to be appointed as a Principal, would not
obligate the State Government to make payment of his salary, on failure of the
Managing Committee to appoint him on a regular basis, in as much as Classes 11
and 12 of the subject institute were never admitted to grant-in-aid. Even if the
review applicant's claim to be appointed as an ad hoc principal is presumed to
have some basis, even then the liability for payment of his salary as a Principal can
only be fastened on the Managing Committee of the subject institute, and not on
the State Government.
9. Under Section 18(1) of the 1982 Act, it is only if the post/vacancy is
sanctioned, would it then be required to be notified to the selection board. Since
the post of Principal, for Classes 11 and 12, has not even been sanctioned by the
State Government, the question of notifying such a post, to be filled up by the
selection board, would not arise.
10. It is only if the order under review suffers from an error apparent on
the face of record, would interference be justified. We find no such infirmity in the
order under review. The review application fails and is, accordingly, dismissed. No
costs.

(Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, C. J.)
 13.09.2019 13.09.2019
NISHANT
